title: Framing of the Constitution and Its Characteristics
shortDescription: Constituent Assembly, Drafting Committee, sources borrowed and salient features.
genZNote: 2 years, 11 months, 18 days: that's how long it took to write India's rulebook. Know who chaired what and what we borrowed from where.

sections.heading: Making of the Constitution
bullets: Constituent Assembly formed under the Cabinet Mission Plan, 1946; first met on 9 December 1946 (Sachchidananda Sinha as provisional president); Dr. Rajendra Prasad elected permanent president on 11 December 1946.
Objectives Resolution moved by Jawaharlal Nehru on 13 December 1946, adopted 22 January 1947.
Drafting Committee set up 29 August 1947 with Dr. B. R. Ambedkar as Chairman; Constitution adopted 26 November 1949 and came into force 26 January 1950 (Republic Day, Purna Swaraj Day link of 1930).
Took about 2 years, 11 months and 18 days; originally 395 Articles, 22 Parts and 8 Schedules; today commonly cited as about 448 Articles, 25 Parts and 12 Schedules.

sections.heading: Salient Characteristics
bullets: Longest written constitution; blend of rigidity and flexibility (Art. 368); federal with unitary bias; parliamentary democracy; fundamental rights with directive principles; independent integrated judiciary; secular; universal adult franchise; single citizenship; emergency provisions; basic structure doctrine (Kesavananda Bharati, 1973).

quickRevision.oneLineDefinition: The Constitution was framed by the Constituent Assembly (1946–49) and combines borrowed features with original adaptations into a federal parliamentary democracy.

highYieldFacts: Rajendra Prasad: president of the Assembly.
commonTraps: Do not say Nehru chaired the Drafting Committee.
